findings.statement: check_ssot_consistency.py's status-token detection (STATUS_RE / STATUS_ANYCASE_RE at lines 337-360, and build_structured_regex at lines 524-554) matches only the literal ASCII bytes of PASS/FAIL/etc. Replacing the status word with a visually identical Cyrillic homoglyph run (U+0420 U+0410 U+0405 U+0405 -- renders as 'PASS' in ordinary fonts) placed beside a real gate id in a live, controlling region produces NO error and NO 'unresolved' entry: exit 0 with output byte-identical to the clean baseline ({"ok": true, "gates": 8, ..., "status_assertions_checked": 25, "gates_covered": 8}). This is not merely a case that gets refused-as-unresolved (the intended fail-closed behavior for anything the checker cannot classify) -- it produces literally zero diagnostic output, because the entire unresolved-detection path in find_assertions() is itself gated on STATUS_ANYCASE_RE finding a literal token first (see the 'if not tokens: continue' at line 985); if the token is invisible to that regex, the id beside it is never even considered. Verified against three independent live-region code paths (overlay_regions in docs/harness/PROJECT_STATE.md and docs/harness/NEXT_SESSION_PROMPT.md, and top_table_row in docs/harness/VALIDATION_LEDGER.md), against both target gates (G-HARNESS-INTEGRITY and G-F10-INDEPENDENT-FLRW, both registry status FAIL), and in both surviving legal-looking forms (free prose next to the id, and the officially-endorsed `ID=STATUS` declaration syntax with the status homoglyphed). All four reproductions gave the identical clean-baseline JSON at exit 0. This directly instantiates the task's target lie: a live handoff surface asserting G-HARNESS-INTEGRITY (or G-F10-INDEPENDENT-FLRW) is PASS while the registry says FAIL, with the checker reporting ok:true.

findings.statement: CONTROL, attack failed as attempted: writing the same Cyrillic homoglyph directly into the Status CELL of the authoritative Gate-board table (docs/harness/PROJECT_STATE.md line 68, the recognised board form the checker's docstring documents) IS caught. find_board_assertions requires the Status cell to reduce to exactly one legible bare token regardless of whether any token is found; zero legible tokens is itself the failure condition, so the homoglyph triggers 'unresolved' -> hard error, not silence. Exact diagnostic: 'docs/harness/PROJECT_STATE.md:68: G-HARNESS-INTEGRITY its Status cell holds no status token. A live surface may state a status only as `G-HARNESS-INTEGRITY=<STATUS>` or as a board table row; prose around a status token is not parsed...'. Exit code 1. This is the asymmetry that makes F-R13-01 possible: board cells are checked unconditionally, but the free-prose/ID=STATUS refusal path only fires once a literal ASCII token is already found beside an id (see F-R13-01), so evading that literal match evades the refusal too, and only free-standing text (not a recognised board cell) is exposed.
